summary: Settlements stopped because order-service deploy dep-6010 (v2.16.0, 07:40Z) changed the OrderExecuted event schema (renamed qty->quantity, header bumped to v2). settlement-service still expects schema v1 and has been failing to deserialize since 07:42Z ('missing required field qty ... schema v1 expected, header says v2'), entering a poison-message retry loop that blocked partition orders-3. Consumption stopped (request_rate 62 -> 0.4 req/s), zero settlements posted, and consumer lag climbed to ~61.6k. The consumer poll config change cfg-3004 (07:35Z) blamed in the report is a red herring: it preceded onset and cannot produce a schema deserialize failure. Root cause originates in the order-service release (bad_deployment); fix is to make settlement-service understand schema v2 (or roll back order-service), then reset the stuck offset.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.16.0 schema change produces records settlement-service cannot deserialize, blocking the partition
ranked_hypotheses.statement: order-service deploy dep-6010 (07:40Z) renamed OrderExecuted.qty to quantity and bumped the schema header to v2. settlement-service still expects v1 and fails to deserialize the first v2 record on partition orders-3 at 07:42Z; the consumer enters a poison-message retry loop and the partition is blocked, so zero settlements post and consumer lag grows unbounded. The fault originates in the order-service release; the consumer poll config change is coincidental.

causal_chain.claim: order-service v2.16.0 deployed at 07:40Z renaming qty->quantity and header v2
settlement-service cannot deserialize v2 OrderExecuted ('missing required field qty, schema v1 expected, header says v2') from 07:42Z
consumer stuck retrying same offset, partition blocked from 07:44Z
consumption stops: request_rate 62->0.4 req/s and consumer_lag climbs to 61605
CPU spikes to ~70% from busy retry loop; no restarts, HTTP error_rate normal

assumptions: The v2 records in orders-3@8841207 were produced by the newly deployed order-service v2.16.0.
settlement-service has not yet been updated to understand schema v2.

ranked_hypotheses.title: settlement-service consumer config change (cfg-3004) caused the stall
ranked_hypotheses.statement: cfg-3004 reduced consumer.max.poll.records from 500 to 200 at 07:35Z, which the report blames for the stall. But the change preceded both the first deserialize error (07:42Z) and the order-service deploy (07:40Z) by several minutes, and the observed failure mode (schema deserialize error + partition block) is unrelated to poll batch size. This hypothesis is rejected.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-3004 applied at 07:35Z reducing poll batch size
No error appears until 07:42Z, after the order-service deploy, so the config change alone does not explain onset
Error is a schema deserialize failure, not a batch-size effect

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Timing does not fit onset (7 min early) and the failure signature (schema deserialize conflict) is unrelated to poll batch size; error began only after the order-service v2 deploy.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka/infrastructure fault (partition reassignment or broker issue) stalled the consumer
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Historical incidents HIST-104/HIST-112 involved consumer stalls after Kafka broker/partition events, which look similar. However kafka logs show only isolated connection-reset retries and no reassignment/error events, notification-service (same broker) is healthy, and the settlement-service errors are explicit schema deserialize failures on a specific record — pointing at a data/schema cause, not infrastructure.

causal_chain.claim: No broker errors or partition reassignment in kafka logs

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No supporting infra telemetry; failure signature is a schema deserialize error, not a broker/rebalance event.

facts.statement: order-service v2.16.0 (dep-6010) deployed at 07:40Z renamed OrderExecuted qty->quantity and set header v2.
settlement-service began failing to deserialize OrderExecuted at 07:42:14Z with 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)'.
From 07:44:51Z settlement-service repeatedly logged 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 ... partition blocked'.
settlement-service request_rate dropped from ~62 to ~0.4 req/s at 07:45Z and consumer_lag rose to 61605 by 09:45Z.
cfg-3004 changed consumer.max.poll.records 500->200 at 07:35Z, before both the first error and the order-service deploy.
settlement-service had zero restarts and normal HTTP error_rate throughout.
kafka, notification-service and payment-service showed no error-level events; only isolated connection-reset retries and a clock-drift warning.
settlement-service CPU rose from ~28% to ~70% during the incident window.
settlement-service and notification-service both consume shared Kafka; order-service produces to it.

assumptions: The v2 record at orders-3@8841207 was produced by order-service v2.16.0 after its 07:40Z rollout.
settlement-service has not been updated for schema v2 (its deserializer still expects v1).
No other producer wrote a malformed record to orders-3; the schema mismatch fully explains the deserialize failure.

timeline.event: order-service v2.16.0 (dep-6010) deployed: OrderExecuted qty->quantity, header v2
settlement-service first deserialize failure on orders-3@8841207 (schema v1 expected, header says v2)
settlement-service poison-message retry loop begins; partition orders-3 blocked
settlement-service request_rate collapses 62 -> 0.4 req/s; CPU rises to ~70%
Incident INC-010 reported (settlements stuck ~40 min, lag 60k)

recommended_actions.action: Make settlement-service able to consume OrderExecuted schema v2 (add quantity field / v2 deserializer) and redeploy; until then, treat the record as skippable rather than blocking the partition.
recommended_actions.rationale: The consumer cannot progress past the v2 record; only schema compatibility unblocks the partition.

recommended_actions.action: If a prompt schema-compatible consumer cannot be shipped, roll back order-service dep-6010 to v2.16.0's predecessor while coordinating the forward fix, and confirm new records revert to a parseable schema.
recommended_actions.rationale: Stops new incompatible records from being produced so the consumer can catch up.

recommended_actions.action: After the fix, reset/seek the stuck offset on orders-3 past 8841207 or DLQ the poison record so the blocked partition resumes.
recommended_actions.rationale: The partition is stuck at a single offset; it will not advance on its own.

recommended_actions.action: Add a schema-compatibility check / canary in the order-service CI-CD pipeline and consumer-side poison-message dead-lettering instead of infinite retry, to prevent a schema change from blocking a partition.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents recurrence of producer/consumer schema mismatch causing a full consumer stall.

recommended_actions.action: Revert or re-evaluate cfg-3004 (poll records 200) only if it is shown to matter; it is not the cause and should not be the primary remediation.
recommended_actions.rationale: Avoid misdirected remediation; the timing and failure signature rule it out as the root cause.

data_gaps: No direct log from order-service confirming it emitted the specific record orders-3@8841207; the link is inferred from the 07:40Z schema-changing deploy and the v2 header in the error.
Settlement lag/partition metrics for other partitions are not shown, so it is unverified whether only orders-3 is blocked or the whole consumer group is affected.
No evidence of whether settlement-service was ever intended to be updated to v2 in the same release train (deploy metadata only lists order-service).
No confirmation of whether a rollback of dep-6010 was attempted; dep-6010 shows status 'live', rolled_back_at null.

findings.statement: order-service deployed v2.16.0 (dep-6010) at 07:40:00Z, which renamed the OrderExecuted field qty -> quantity and set event schema version header to v2.

refs.quote: OrderExecuted event: rename field qty -> quantity

findings.statement: settlement-service began emitting deserialize errors at 07:42:14Z: 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' on partition orders-3@8841207 — ~2 minutes after the order-service deploy.

refs.quote: failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)

findings.statement: From 07:44:51Z settlement-service logged a repeating poison-message loop on the same offset with 'partition blocked', showing the consumer group cannot progress past the bad record.

refs.quote: poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt 92490), partition blocked

findings.statement: settlement-service request_rate collapsed from ~62 req/s to ~0.4 req/s in the 07:45 bucket and stayed flat, while consumer_lag rose from ~42 (07:15) to 61605 (09:45).

The config change cfg-3004 on settlement-service (consumer.max.poll.records 500 -> 200) was applied at 07:35:00Z, ~7 minutes BEFORE the first deserialize error and ~5 minutes before the order-service deploy.
settlement-service had zero restarts and normal HTTP error_rate (~0.2%) throughout, so the failure is a blocked consumer thread, not an HTTP-serving failure or a crash/restart.

Kafka, notification-service and payment-service show no error-level events in the window; only isolated 'connection reset' retries and one clock-drift warning. No shared-infrastructure fault is evident.

refs.quote: retrying idempotent request (attempt 2) after connection reset
clock drift 38ms detected, resyncing with NTP

findings.statement: settlement-service CPU rose from ~28% to ~70% starting in the 07:30-07:45 buckets, consistent with the consumer busy-spinning retrying the same poison record.

settlement-service consumes from shared Kafka (also consumed by notification-service and produced by order-service/payment-service), so the order-service schema change propagates to settlement-service over Kafka.
